overview: A 1945-compiled list indexes 1930 reports on Japanese station JAA interfering with U.S. naval station NPO at Cavite, with instructions to raise it via Tokyo; an unrelated second page reports Japan's Rationalization Bureau discussing a joint government-private steel company modeled on the South Manchuria Railway.

people.name: Edwin L. Neville
people.role: U.S. diplomatic official associated with despatch no. 664 from Japan; no title is stated on the sheet

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning interference between radio stations JAA and NPO
subfiles.about: An index sheet summarizes two January 8, 1930 communications about interference caused by the Japanese station JAA to the U.S. naval station NPO at Cavite.
subfiles.summary: 1930 interference from Japanese station JAA with U.S. naval station NPO at Cavite prompted instructions to press Japan via Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Report fragment on rationalization of the Japanese steel industry
subfiles.about: A brief unattributed report describes a proposal for a joint government-private company to rationalize the steel industry.
subfiles.summary: Japan's Industrial Rationalization Bureau advisers discussed forming a joint government-private steel company modeled on the South Manchuria Railway Company, anticipating a study committee.

interest: Shows a 1930 Japan-U.S. radio-frequency dispute at Cavite, and an unrelated steel-industry rationalization report.
